cohort: The study included 300 participants from Babylon Governorate hospitals, comprising 150 women who delivered by cesarean section (cases) and 150 who delivered vaginally (controls), matched for demographic characteristics.
finding: Key predictors of cesarean delivery included a history of previous CS, prolonged labor, pregnancy complications, non-cephalic fetal presentation, primiparity, overweight maternal BMI, and labor induction, with cesarean deliveries being associated with higher rates of surgical complications, delayed breastfeeding initiation, and increased hospital readmissions.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries were associated with adverse short-term postpartum effects including higher rates of surgical complications, delayed breastfeeding initiation, and increased hospital readmissions.
